chunks: But take care that this should not be done inappropriately, and that you should not behave so with an undeserving person.
Do not take the enemy of your friend as a friend because you will thus antagonize your friend.
Give true advice to your brother, be it good or bitter.
Swallow your anger because I did not find a sweeter thing than it in the end, and nothing more pleasant in consequence.
Be lenient to him who is harsh to you for it is likely that he will shortly become lenient to you.
Treat your enemy with favours, because this is sweeter of the two successes (the success of revenge and the success of doing favour).
If you intend to cut yourself off from a friend leave some scope for him from your side by which he may resume friendship if it occurs to him some day.
If anyone has a good idea about you prove it to be true.
ai.seo_question: What are the key principles of social etiquette and friendship in Imam Ali's instructions to Hasan?
ai.summary: Delivered during the pivotal post-Siffin period, this passage reflects Imam Ali’s strategic wisdom in consolidating social bonds amidst political turbulence, emphasizing that emotional discipline (tadabbur) and magnanimity are superior to mere victory. It underscores the Shia ethical ideal of 'mu'amalat' (social conduct) where one preserves relationships by offering sincere counsel and treating adversaries with grace, thereby turning potential enemies into allies.
